_comment: Single source of truth for all cross-cutting values. Read by validate-contracts, bootstraps, and runtime scripts. Edit THIS file — the manifest installs it to VMs.
_budget_posture: A bound exists to stop an UNBOUNDED blowup, not to save money. Agent success is worth far more than tokens, so every char/token budget here is sized for the work to succeed and only then bounded. The evidence runs both ways and both lessons are load-bearing: an uncapped readFile once pushed a single organ call to 877k input tokens (so caps stay, and every cap ANNOUNCES itself so an organ can re-derive instead of assuming it saw everything) — while a stingy cap silently truncated the Drive listing that held the right template, and the mission built three documents from the wrong one (so caps are generous). Subagent organs run on a 1,048,576-token context window; operating at 10% of it and paying for that in truncation-shaped failures was a bad trade. HARD CEILINGS THAT ARE NOT ABOUT COST, and must not be raised: dispatch.context_token_budget <= 125000 because _accumulated_context persists on the Firestore work document (1 MiB) and budget x 4 chars must fit inside it; compaction.working_budget_tokens <= dispatch.context_token_budget by the same argument. validate-contracts enforces both, and it caught a 500000 attempt made in exactly the generous spirit above — generosity stops where a storage limit starts. ONE ABSOLUTE RULE: nothing here may become unbounded. dispatch.verify_prompt_max_chars was briefly cut to 6000 to dodge a provider malformed-call threshold, and that was a cautionary tale: dodging one failure mode by starving evidence bought a worse one. But the REAL fix was neither a generous cap (24000 still hit MALFORMED at 13K) nor a stingy one — it was switching the evidence SOURCE from verbose motor output to compact result packets, which contain the tool results the verifier needs at a fraction of the size. The cap is now 9000 and first-attempt evidence is compact; full motor output is reserved for the missing-evidence re-verify path, bounded dynamically. See _verify_prompt_comment.

vertex._strong_model_comment: Phase E (CR-9): mechanism to route the planning/execution organs (prefrontal, motor) to the stronger `subagentStrong` (gemini-2.5-pro). Wired end-to-end (config.mjs picks subagentStrong when opts.strong; the gateway sets strong for agents in this list, or when a caller passes strong:true; a strong request wins over a per-agent workspace model pin). Currently DISABLED (empty list → whole fleet stays on flash): a live canary showed pro improves planning coherence (removed a hallucinated premise, correct state assessment) but adds ~10x latency and did NOT close a hard 2-agent code+deploy mission that is ALSO blocked by failure-memory over-planning (CR-8) and motor git/firebase command reliability. Re-enabling is a cost/latency decision — put the agent ids back in this list.

gateway._loop_guard_comment: Stuck-loop bounds. duplicate_* count identical ARGUMENTS (cannot distinguish a pointless repeat from legitimate polling). identical_result_* count byte-identical RESULTS for the same arguments — a proven no-op, so bounded tighter. semantic_* bound the varying-arguments case, where a lone nudge was demonstrably ignorable.

tools._comment: Gateway tool-result discipline (B-4). A tool result IS context: bound it, ANNOUNCE the bound so the organ can re-derive instead of assuming it saw everything, and never let a binary file reach a model. An unbounded readFile on a downloaded PDF once pushed a single organ call to 877k input tokens.

versioning._comment: Canonical commit format: v{YYYY}.{MM}.{DD}.{index}.{subindex}: description. This is the FOREVER format. The extractVersion() regex in app/src/app/api/upgrade/route.ts MUST match this. A temporary vX.Y.Z format was used during v5.0-v5.3 and is supported for back-compat only.

dispatch._verify_full_evidence_comment: Ceiling for the ONE re-verification triggered when a FAIL cites missing evidence OR when the executor KNOWS it fed the verifier a truncated view (compact > evidence budget). The executor now binds this knob under a prompt-safe budget (verify_prompt_max_chars - criteria - boilerplate) and reduces the evidence shape-aware (packToolEvidence keeps every tool RESULT, not a head+tail clip that drops the middle). Prior bug: a hardcoded '9000 - criteria' cap made this value DEAD (it never bound) and starved the re-verify to ~6.5K — the same truncation that caused the FAIL. Raising it above what the verifier model can ingest is a contract + model change (Gemini Flash MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL), not a code change.
dispatch._recovered_tool_error_comment: detectMotorFailure matches a failure pattern (e.g. 'command failed') ANYWHERE in the motor's output. A multi-command task can have one sub-command error and still finish with the full deliverable in its prose answer — hard-failing that blocked a discovery mission that had gathered everything. When true, a failure marker confined to the [TOOL EXECUTION LOG] (with a substantive, non-failing answer beside it) is annotated for cerebellum to arbitrate (B-28), not hard-failed. When false, the strict any-substring hard-fail returns. A failure marker in the ANSWER prose, or a thin/absent answer, still hard-fails either way.
dispatch._verify_prompt_comment: Lowered 24000 -> 9000 and switched the first attempt from full motor output to compact result packets. The previous 24000 cap produced prompts of ~13K chars that hit MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL deterministically. The 6000 over-correction starved evidence because it used the SAME verbose motor output — the real fix is a different evidence SOURCE, not a different cap. Compact evidence (result packets, already capped at ctx_agent_step=8000/task) contains the tool results the verifier actually needs; the verbose motor reasoning is noise for verification. Full motor output is still available in the missing-evidence re-verify path, bounded to stay under the MALFORMED threshold.
dispatch._spine_comment: A checkpoint failure re-plans that checkpoint, not the mission. Outcomes are stable in practice (four observed missions never changed them) while task lists churn — and re-deriving the whole plan once re-ran a checkpoint that had PASSED twenty seconds earlier, at a cost of 1.11M input tokens. spine_pinning holds outcomes+verdicts; criteria_pinning holds the wording, allowing max_criteria_revisions refinements (evidence both ways: one mission passed only after a rewording, another reworded four times without converging). Cortex can still force a full re-shape via replan_scope:'mission' — logged as spine_replaced.
dispatch._pass_replan_comment: Two guards against re-planning verified work — the elision churn where a read-only discovery re-shaped its already-PASSED checkpoint 5+ times (52 calls / 1.4M tokens) because its data rode as a ref Cortex never hydrated. pass_synthesize_nudge: after a passed plan, steer Cortex to synthesize (or hydrate a ref), where today success gets no nudge. reject_full_replan_when_passing: refuse a replan_scope:'mission' re-shape when every checkpoint passed and none failed — deliver or escalate, never re-shape verified work. Both revert to prior behavior when false.
dispatch._blocked_blocker_comment: A milestone-verification verdict judges a checkpoint, not the mission's deliverable. A real report_fail (not merely inconclusive) on a checkpoint whose TASKS all succeeded once terminated a FINISHED mission as `blocked`, with the mission's own success summary written into the blocker field — a complete 2-page flyer PDF delivered to the operator as an on_failure outcome. When true: before finalizing an M-type mission as `blocked` (blocked.mjs), and before the self-unblock upgrade in synthesize_with_failure, the daemon checks whether any real dispatched TASK actually failed — excluding cerebellum `*.verify` pseudo-steps and inconclusive/timed-out rows (the same exclusion synthesize.mjs applies). If none failed and a deliverable exists, `blocked` is a mislabel and the mission is re-routed ONCE to a verified synthesize (B-28) instead. A genuine external blocker still blocks: a failed task, or an explicit non-'other' blocker_type (access/permission/auth/missing-input/external/dependency/quota/rate-limit). One-shot + iteration-bounded. Reverts to prior behavior when false.
dispatch._delegation_capability_guard_comment: A delegation must not hand a teammate work its specialty cannot do while the delegator's own specialty can. Observed live: a devops agent delegated a Firebase DEPLOY (its own work) to an engineer with no deploy skill, and the engineer blocked (`Unknown blocker`), then the mission failed. When true: before dispatching a cross-agent delegation, the executor compares the target specialty's skills (agent-types.json) to the delegator's; if the task instruction explicitly invokes a distinctive capability the target lacks but the delegator owns (a skill/CLI id like `firebase`/`gcloud`/`docker`, matched as a standalone token, not a filename), the delegation is redirected to a local motor task the delegating agent executes itself. Direction-aware (only fires when work is sent AWAY from the agent that can do it) and conservative (only on an explicit capability token). Complements the ownership-routing guidance (a part your own capabilities cover is `local`, never delegated). Reverts to prior behavior when false.
dispatch._specialty_deploy_honesty_comment: Generic fix for the observed false-complete: a product-architect/PM agent given 'update the site + deploy to a Firebase staging preview, share the URL' completed 7/7 with NO delegation, NO deploy permission used, and NO URL. Four layer-pure brain-code guards, all default on (revert = false), classification of what is destructive lives in the organ SOUL not here (C-28): (1) execution_capability_reroute — the mirror of delegation_capability_guard: a LOCAL motor task that invokes a distinctive capability THIS agent's specialty lacks but a project teammate's specialty owns (e.g. `firebase` on a product-architect) is converted to a delegation to the owner, on BOTH the checkpoint_plan and follow_process paths (checkExecutionCapability). (2) process_checkpoint_verification — the process→checkpoint conversion synthesizes a real checkpoint accept_criteria from its grouped steps instead of the historical '' that DISARMED cerebellum verification, so a process mission can no longer false-complete (synthesizeCheckpointCriterion). (3) publish_soft_pass_guard — a delivery-critical (deploy/publish/promote) task whose command failed cannot soft-pass on prose length alone (only on proven retry-recovery), closing the path where a failed deploy with confident narrative reported ✅ (isDeliveryCriticalIntent + isRecoveredToolError requireActionRecovery). (4) irreversibility_guard_bounded — the checkpoint_plan approval-gate nudge fires at most once per mission instead of unboundedly, so it can no longer burn every iteration and force a follow_process fallback that runs the risky action unverified.
dispatch._delegation_model_comment: Delegation MODEL. 'child-mission' (default, current behavior): a delegation spawns a SEPARATE mission on the delegate (materializeDelegationMission) and only a summarized result returns. 'handoff' (baton): ONE mission travels agent->agent — the delegate works the SAME work/{id} (its assigned checkpoints on the shared _cp_spine) and hands the same mission back, so context AND the mission/<id> git branch travel natively. Routing keys on the envelope: assignee (whose turn it is) vs originator (who started it); each _cp_spine[n].assignee tags a checkpoint. Decision logic is pure in corekit/lib/baton.mjs; see docs/plans/DELEGATION_HANDOFF_PLAN.md. Flag-gated so both models coexist during rollout — flip to 'handoff' per-fleet after canary.
dispatch._project_bootstrap_comment: Fleet PROJECT BOOTSTRAP. When enabled, a PM/lead role (has the project-ops skill) may choose the project_bootstrap action to stand up a whole delivery project from a chat ask: the GChat space the ask arrived on becomes the project's comms space, the team is seeded (emails resolved from the fleet roster), and the mission is re-scoped to the new project so its delegations route through that space. Handler: corekit/daemon/actions/project_bootstrap.mjs; pure core corekit/lib/project-bootstrap.mjs; see docs/plans/PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP_PLAN.md. Adding the delegate bots as space MEMBERS stays an operator action (no chat.memberships scope). Default off; enable per-VM for canary via AGENT_PROJECT_BOOTSTRAP=on, or flip here after canary.
dispatch._delivery_robustness_comment: Two guards for multi-agent DELIVERY, from a live 1health mission that false-completed: archie re-delegated a design review ~6x over 35 min (the delegate's input branch was empty), then SYNTHESIZED `complete` with 3 of 4 checkpoints still pending and an empty deliverable — a false green. finalize_requires_spine_complete (FC-A, synthesize.mjs): a mission with a pinned _cp_spine may not synthesize COMPLETE while its DELIVERABLE (last) checkpoint is unmet — it fails closed to needs_input naming what's outstanding. redelegation_cap_enabled (FC-B, agent-brain.mjs checkWaitingEnvelopes): a checkpoint whose delegation returns with failures is re-delegated at most redelegation_max times; past that the mission escalates to the operator (needs_input) instead of looping. Both were PROVEN on the archie delivery-robustness canary, and the deploy-delegation canary (2026-08-10) then showed that with delegation now the norm, a delegate that cannot converge makes the delegator re-delegate UNBOUNDED — exactly what FC-B caps — so both are now default ON here. The AGENT_FINALIZE_SPINE_GUARD / AGENT_REDELEG_CAP env vars still override per-VM. Both fire only on a pinned-spine mission with an unmet deliverable / a repeatedly-failing delegation. Revert = false.
dispatch._nonterminal_milestone_nonhalt_comment: FC-D (checkpoint-executor.mjs, pure checkpointFailureHalts in checkpoint-spine.mjs): a live 1health 'change the hero + give me a staging link' mission delivered the outcome (deploy checkpoint served the change on staging) but re-planned to iteration 8 without completing, because an upstream EDIT checkpoint's milestone kept 'failing' — the edit was made by a DELEGATE (bobby) in the delegate's own workspace/branch, invisible to the delegator's (archie's) cerebellum verification, so a clean edit read as a FAIL, halted the plan (executor break) and looped. When ON, a NON-terminal checkpoint whose TASKS all succeeded but whose MILESTONE could not be confirmed does not HALT the mission — it is flagged needs_review and the plan proceeds so the DELIVERABLE (terminal) checkpoint runs and its OBSERVABLE milestone (a reachable URL) gates. A real task failure, or any failure on the terminal checkpoint, still halts (fail-closed, B-28/FC-A preserved). Opt-in (changes halt semantics); PROVEN on the archie->bobby->stan canary (reprove#2/#3: fired as nonterminal_milestone_nonhalt, spine advanced, no reset-loop, honesty held) and ENABLED fleet-wide.
dispatch._skip_advances_spine_comment: FC-E (checkpoint-executor.mjs skip path): sibling of FC-D, the OTHER half of the same reset-loop. When a checkpoint RESUMES with all its tasks already banked (the delegation-resume case — the delegate's child completed), the executor skips re-running the tasks. That skip marked the child envelope complete but did NOT write the pinned spine, so the spine entry stayed 'pending'. firstIncompleteIndex() returns the first non-'complete' entry, so a later re-plan (e.g. the terminal checkpoint failing verification) re-targeted the already-done EDIT/DEPLOY checkpoint and the executor restarted the whole mission from it — re-running a completed edit/deploy forever (observed on the clean-baseline reprove: pinned spine read [pending,pending,failed] though CP1 edit + CP2 deploy were done). When ON, the skip advances the spine (marks the checkpoint complete). Honest because a skip means the tasks SUCCEEDED (a failed task/milestone clears the step-ledger so it re-runs, never skips), delegated completions are re-derived at the resume seam (WS-3), and the terminal deliverable is re-derived again at synthesize (mandatory for delegated outcomes) before the mission is reported complete. Opt-in; PROVEN on the archie->bobby->stan canary (reprove#3: spine_status 'status=complete (tasks-banked skip)' fired, scoped re-plan preserved completed verdicts, no reset-loop) and ENABLED fleet-wide.
dispatch._probe_gated_finalize_comment: FC-F (synthesize.mjs, pure probeGatedFinalizeAction in checkpoint-spine.mjs): refines the FC-A finalize gate (finalize_requires_spine_complete) so it can't produce a FALSE-NEGATIVE. FC-A blocks a synthesize→complete while the SPINE says the deliverable checkpoint is unmet — but the spine is bookkeeping, not ground truth. Observed (reprove#3): a delegated 'change the hero → give me a staging link' mission put the new hero LIVE on staging (curl 200), cortex wrote the correct answer + URL, yet FC-A blocked finalize because a LATER re-plan had re-tasked the deploy onto archie's OWN motor (no Firebase perms → 'Command failed'), marking the terminal checkpoint 'failed' — so the mission churned to iter 9+ though its deliverable was met. When ON, and the mission rests on a DELEGATED observable deliverable, the spine-based block is DEFERRED to the mandatory delegated-outcome re-derivation the synthesize verify already runs (cerebellum re-derives the artifact via request_probe, B-28), and re-applied FAIL-CLOSED unless that re-derivation explicitly PASSES: live→PASS→finalize (false-negative fixed); genuinely missing→FAIL→synthesize_with_failure; inconclusive/no-verdict→needs_input (fail-closed, exactly as FC-A). No false-POSITIVE: only an OBSERVED re-derivation PASS unblocks. Opt-in; default OFF until proven on canary; AGENT_PROBE_GATED_FINALIZE=1 per-VM env for canary.
dispatch._verify_probe_comment: DORMANT — not read by the executor. A probe lets a verifier ask for evidence it lacks, but nothing ever serviced a returned request (extractProbes was imported and never called), so advertising request_probe produced verifiers that asked a question we could not answer, and the B-28 fail-closed then failed the milestone for asking it. The scaffolding is out of the verify prompt until the probe loop exists; these flags are kept so re-enabling is one change, and left here rather than deleted so the intent is not lost.

_brain_comment: Per-task tool-call budget for EXECUTION agents (motor/cerebellum/temporal-research) in the neural gateway (corekit/brain/config.mjs maxSteps). DISTINCT from dispatch.max_iterations (the mission decide-loop cap). Absent until now → config.mjs fell back to 12, too tight for a full coding task (read files → edit → serve+verify → work-diff → commit exceeds 12 and fails mid-way, forcing the re-plan churn seen in the bobby coding loop). Raised to 25: comfortable headroom, still inside the 300s per-task timeout; cerebellum/research stop early on their own regardless. See docs/plans/CODING_RELIABILITY_PLAN.md CR-2.

delivery._comment: Mouth delivery retry discipline: exponential backoff between failed attempts, terminal delivery_status='failed' at max_attempts. Brain fast-fails waiting delegation Ts off the terminal status.

organ_context._tool_answer_min_prose_comment: For a tool-agent result, prose OUTSIDE the [TOOL EXECUTION LOG] below this many chars means the tool RESULTS are the answer (a discovery mission), so the packet summary digests those results instead of eliding the log to a bare marker. Above it (an edit confirmation, an audit verdict), the prose is the answer and the log is elided for economy. The defect this gates: a 2.6KB discovery result collapsed to a 53-char '[tool log elided]' marker, so Cortex saw no data and re-planned.

memory._comment: Memory subsystem knobs. resource_ledger: an external identifier (Drive folder/doc id, chat space) is a fact about the world that does not change — resolve it once, remember it, never search again. Capture is deterministic from structured tool output (C-4/C-5) and lands on the mission envelope in Firestore, so it survives a resume that re-clones and destroys the working tree. Surfacing is memory's job: recall Layer E offers it to temporal-memory, which remains the sole producer of the packet the brain sees.

resource_ledger._promotion: Promotion into the durable `resources` category is TEMPORAL-MEMORY's job, done during consolidation (memory-consolidate SKILL step 5b) — not a daemon auto-write. v2026.06.21.1.0 deliberately removed daemon writes to core memory as noise, and temporal-memory is the memory authority and sole memory mutator. The daemon only captures to the envelope; within-mission and across-resume reuse works from there immediately, and cross-mission reuse lands at the next consolidation.

workspaces._comment: Canonical workspace directories the daemon reads from. Manifests MUST target these paths.

git._comment: Tenant-internal git artifact substrate. Single bucket, per-repo prefixes. ADC via metadata SA token.
